svg.title: Plant health
svg.desc: Plant infections: TMV: virus; mosaic leaf discolouration → less photosynthesis/growth. Limit transfer from infected plants/tools. Rose black spot: fungus; purple/black spots, yellow leaves, early leaf fall → less photosynthesis. Wind/water spread spores; remove affected leaves or use fungicides. Pests & symptoms: Aphids feed on sugar-rich sap, reducing growth; may transmit viruses. Look for stunted growth, spots, decay, growths, malformed stems/leaves, discolouration and pests. A symptom alone may have several possible causes. Mineral deficiencies: Nitrate: needed for amino acids/proteins. Shortage → stunted growth. Magnesium: needed for chlorophyll. Shortage → chlorosis and reduced photosynthesis. Deficiencies are not communicable; mineral supply will not cure a virus. Identify the problem: Compare symptoms with reliable gardening references. Laboratories identify pathogens; monoclonal-antibody kits test for specific targets. Combine evidence; a negative test for one pathogen does not rule out other causes. Physical & chemical: Cellulose cell walls, tough waxy cuticle and dead bark resist entry. Shedding bark can remove pathogens. Antibacterial chemicals act against bacteria. Poisons deter herbivores. Mechanical adaptations: Thorns and hairs deter feeding. Leaves may droop or curl when touched. Mimicry tricks animals into avoiding plants. Link each feature to how it protects.
